owner.name: Estela Pérez Luque
owner.title: Senior Data Scientist | Predictive Modelling & Systems Validation

philosophy: I believe in the importance of having rigorous frameworks to evaluate systems and a comprehensive understanding to connect the dots. I am driven to solve real-world problems by understanding customer needs and providing the best solutions through deep system analysis.
resumeProfile: Senior data scientist with a PhD in Informatics and 5+ years of experience building predictive models, validation pipelines, and data-driven systems for complex engineering challenges. I design reproducible end-to-end analysis workflows that turn experimental and simulation data into traceable evidence for engineering decisions and system improvement. I lead cross-functional projects across industry, international research, and startup ventures—translating complex technical findings into actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

bullets: Built end-to-end Python and MATLAB pipelines for simulation validation and model benchmarking, comparing prediction outputs against motion capture and in-vehicle datasets using RMSE, DTW, and Bland-Altman metrics—producing reproducible, traceable evidence for engineering decisions and test planning.

Led multi-stakeholder R&D projects with Volvo Cars, Volvo Trucks, Scania, Texas Tech University, and University of Antwerp, aligning scope, timelines, and expectations across technical and non-technical teams and translating findings into decision-ready reports, resulting in 15+ peer-reviewed publications.

Applied multi-objective optimization (NSGA-II) to vehicle interior design problems, evaluating 1,000+ configurations across 14 digital human manikins—shifting ergonomics assessment from manual trial-and-error to systematic, scalable design-space exploration.

Designed and executed experimental studies with motion capture and 4D body-scanning systems across diverse applications, managing protocol development, ethics approvals, and data pipelines from scratch to publication-ready outputs.
Supervised 10+ BSc theses and delivered teaching at BSc and MSc level; elected Student Representative and Board Member representing 40+ PhD students in university-level research governance.

Managed a 6-month international research stay end-to-end: led ethics application for 5-year large-scale data collection approval, designed motion capture and 4D body-scanning protocols for 30+ participants, and built reproducible multi-site data pipelines enabling consistent validation across institutions.

experience.company: Swe-Ex AB (Startup) — Science Park Skövde, Sweden
bullets: Co-founded an early-stage wearable technology startup developing exoskeleton-inspired safety support equipment for assembly-line environments, incubated at Science Park Skövde over 2 years.

Translated user needs and safety requirements into measurable product targets and drove three full prototype iterations from CAD to physical validation using 3D-printed, textile, and steel components.

Built commercial acumen through investor communications, market analysis across 10+ industries, and structured business planning—bridging technical capability with product viability and go-to-market strategy.

Contributed to applied projects with 6+ industry partners: conducted ergonomic assessments (RULA, REBA), produced decision-ready analytical reports and educational content, and presented findings to cross-functional teams to support product development decisions.

projects.title: PhD Thesis: Human Posture & Motion Prediction
projects.tagline: A comprehensive framework for automotive ergonomics design through 6 interconnected research papers.
projects.summary: This thesis represents a multi-year journey to improve digital human modelling tools. It connects 6 distinct research papers into a cohesive methodology for predicting and validating human movement in vehicles.
projects.challenge: Ergonomics tools often lack the behavioral realism and validation needed for early-stage automotive design decisions.
projects.solution: Developed a suite of methods ranging from workflow mapping to multi-objective optimization and motion capture validation.
whatIDid: Led the end-to-end research lifecycle for 6 international publications
Developed novel 3D predictive frameworks using Python, MATLAB, and DHM tools
Validated simulation models against large-scale real-world driver datasets
impact: Created a bridge between virtual ergonomics and measured human behaviour
Demonstrated scalable ways to treat ergonomics as an optimization problem
Provided industry-ready benchmarks for choosing posture prediction methods

projects.title: Mapped Ergonomics Workflows in Automotive Development
projects.tagline: Studied how ergonomics teams work in vehicle development and where current tools slow down better decisions.
projects.summary: Interview-based project focused on how ergonomics is actually handled in Swedish automotive product development, from requirements and trade-offs to tools and validation.
projects.challenge: Ergonomics teams need to balance comfort, visibility, posture, safety, manufacturing, and styling, but current workflows and tools make early ergonomics work slower, more fragmented, and harder to scale.
projects.solution: Ran a structured interview study with ergonomics specialists across Swedish automotive companies to map workflows, tool usage, pain points, and capability gaps.
whatIDid: Designed and ran a semi-structured interview study with ergonomics professionals
Analysed workflows, tool use, decision points, and recurring bottlenecks
Translated findings into concrete improvement areas for digital ergonomics tools
impact: Identified four clear opportunity areas: behavior prediction, tool usability, ergonomics evaluation methods, and better integration between systems
Created a grounded industry picture of how ergonomics is handled in real vehicle programs
Provided the practical foundation for the later simulation and prediction work in the thesis

evidence.publicationTitle: Challenges for the Consideration of Ergonomics in Product Development in the Swedish Automotive Industry – An Interview Study

projects.title: Improved How Virtual Drivers Are Positioned in the Seat
projects.tagline: Developed a more realistic way to align digital humans to vehicle seating geometry.
projects.summary: Focused on a core simulation problem in occupant packaging: the mismatch between vehicle reference points like the H-point and the human anatomical hip joint used in DHM tools.
projects.challenge: Current seated posture workflows often depend on manual adjustment because standard vehicle reference points do not map cleanly to biomechanical human models.
projects.solution: Developed the Body Shape Alignment method, using a virtual H-point machine template to align manikin body surfaces more consistently to the seat and compare it against a statistical prediction approach.
whatIDid: Investigated the relationship between vehicle seating reference points and human hip-joint location
Built the Body Shape Alignment concept for seated driving simulations
Compared the new method against a statistical prediction approach using realistic body meshes
impact: Showed a more consistent and realistic positioning approach across body types
Reduced dependence on purely manual seat alignment in virtual posture setup
Improved repeatability and communication of seating assumptions in occupant packaging studies

evidence.publicationTitle: Simulation of Hip Joint Location for Occupant Packaging Design

projects.title: Automated Vehicle Packaging Trade-Offs with Multi-Objective Optimization
projects.tagline: Built a workflow that explores seat and steering wheel design options automatically instead of by manual trial and error.
projects.summary: Combined digital human modelling with simulation-based multi-objective optimization to explore occupant packaging decisions across a diverse user population.
projects.challenge: Occupant packaging requires balancing multiple competing ergonomics targets and geometric constraints, but traditional workflows are too manual to explore the design space well.
projects.solution: Integrated a DHM tool with a multi-objective optimization workflow using NSGA-II, allowing thousands of design variants to be generated and assessed automatically.
whatIDid: Defined the optimization problem, variables, objectives, and constraints for an occupant packaging scenario
Built a simulation loop using 14 digital manikins to represent anthropometric diversity
Used NSGA-II to evaluate 1000 design variants in a structured way
impact: Shifted ergonomics assessment toward systematic design-space exploration
Reduced manual iteration and improved traceability in design evaluation
Demonstrated a scalable way to treat ergonomics as an optimization problem earlier in development

evidence.publicationTitle: Simulation-based Multi-objective Optimization Combined with a DHM tool for Occupant Packaging Design

projects.title: Benchmarked Two Driving Posture Prediction Methods with Real Vehicle Data
projects.tagline: Compared statistical and optimization-based posture prediction methods using real users in two vehicle layouts.
projects.summary: Evaluated two seated driving posture prediction approaches against real-world data collected from 199 drivers across two Volvo vehicle models with different seat heights.
projects.challenge: DHM posture prediction methods are often used in industry without enough evidence of how they behave in different vehicle configurations.
projects.solution: Compared a Statistical Prediction Method (SPM) and an Optimization Prediction Method (OPM) for H-point, eye-point, and steering wheel prediction, using real measured data as ground truth.
whatIDid: Worked with real-world driving posture data from 199 participants
Compared SPM and OPM across key driver position variables
Analysed errors across fore-aft and vertical dimensions and by vehicle configuration
impact: Showed that OPM performed better for H-point x and steering wheel x across both vehicles
Showed that SPM performed better for H-point z across both vehicles
Provided a practical basis for choosing prediction methods by context instead of treating one method as universally best

evidence.publicationTitle: A case study of digital human modelling assisted occupant packaging design: comparing driving posture and position prediction methods

projects.title: Used Simulation Plus Real Data to Tailor Posture Prediction Models
projects.tagline: Expanded incomplete driver datasets into more useful posture prediction strategies for different stature groups.
projects.summary: Developed a process to enhance seated driver posture prediction by combining real-world driving position data with simulation outputs and extracted joint-angle information.
projects.challenge: In occupant packaging, teams often have only partial real-world data, which limits how well they can improve or tailor posture prediction models.
projects.solution: Built a three-step process: collect driver position data, generate matching manikins, and simulate them in their preferred positions to extract more complete posture information.
whatIDid: Integrated seat position, steering wheel position, and eye-point data with simulation
Generated manikins matched to participant anthropometry
Extracted joint-angle information from simulated seated postures
Built stature-based posture strategies for short, medium, and tall drivers
impact: Showed that stature-based strategies improved prediction for short and tall driver groups
Demonstrated a practical way to extend incomplete posture datasets
Supported more customized posture prediction instead of relying on one generic default strategy

evidence.publicationTitle: Improving Occupant Packaging Posture Prediction Through Integration of Simulation and Real Data

projects.title: Compared Optimization and Heuristic Models for 3D Reaching Motion
projects.tagline: Evaluated which motion prediction approach works better for path, velocity, and arm configuration in seated reaching tasks.
projects.summary: Compared an optimization-based method with a new heuristic pipeline for predicting upper-extremity reaching motions in 3D space.
projects.challenge: Human motion prediction methods tend to trade off precision, behavioural realism, and variability, making it difficult to choose the right method for simulation applications.
projects.solution: Benchmarked an optimization-based method against a heuristic method combining steering dynamics, adaptive velocity modelling, and FABRIK inverse kinematics.
whatIDid: Developed and tested the heuristic Steering-FABRIK Method (SFM)
Compared SFM with an optimization-based method (OPM)
Evaluated path, velocity, and arm joint configuration separately
Used RMSE and DTW to assess both error magnitude and motion-shape similarity
Analysed how well each model captured inter-subject variability
impact: Showed that SFM performed better for path prediction and velocity shape
Showed that OPM performed better for arm joint configuration accuracy
Made the trade-off between prediction precision and behavioural diversity more explicit for future DHM applications

evidence.publicationTitle: Predicting Human Upper Extremity Reaching Motions: Comparison of Optimization-based Method and Heuristic Method

projects.title: Built Motion Capture-Based Validation Workflows
projects.tagline: Used optical motion capture and structured task design to generate ground-truth data for validating posture and motion models.
projects.summary: Hands-on experimental work around motion capture and measured human movement, used to evaluate prediction methods rather than relying only on simulation outputs.
projects.challenge: Simulation methods are only useful if they can be checked against real human behaviour with enough precision and repeatability.
projects.solution: Used motion capture and structured data collection protocols to create validation datasets for both seated posture and upper-extremity reaching tasks.
whatIDid: Worked with recorded driving posture data from real users in two vehicle models
Used motion capture data from seated reaching tasks as validation ground truth
Applied quantitative metrics such as RMSE, DTW, correlation, and Bland-Altman analysis to compare prediction outputs to measured behaviour
impact: Strengthened the credibility of the prediction and simulation work
Created a bridge between virtual ergonomics and measured human behaviour
Enabled more rigorous comparison of competing modelling approaches

evidence.notes: Based on the thesis methodology and datasets used to validate seated posture and reaching-motion prediction methods.
